properties.state: {"description":"DesignEpoch.status carries `planned` (a claim about a point that has not happened) or `arrived` (a record of one that has), with plan_epoch to create the forward kind and set_epoch_status to move between them. Status is a property in its own right rather than a value in epoch_type, because kind and tense are orthogonal — a planned MILESTONE and a planned RELEASE CUT are both sayable, and those are the two a roadmap is made of. It mirrors Release.status, which already carries `planned` for the capability view. The default is `arrived`, which is a record rather than a choice (req:defaults-do-not-assert): add_epoch's 27 call sites have only ever meant recording the point you are at, so every epoch written before the property existed did arrive. THE LOAD-BEARING HALF IS THE REFUSAL — record_change rejects a planned epoch, because a snapshot captures the present and cannot belong to a point that has not happened. Without it, status would be a declared-and-unconsulted field: stored, never read, true only by politeness. Delivered 2026-07-30 in 56a8388; both guards mutation-tested rather than merely covered, since a test that still passes with the check deleted is not evidence the check works.","is_entry_point":false,"is_exit_point":false,"name":"An epoch can be planned, and arrival is the event that makes it history","provenance":"authored","status":"realized","tier":"operational"}
